title: Harden refusal messages: bounded token echo, literal-dollar wording, first-denial priority, literal pins
judge_obligation_ack: standard lane: feature-close independent review pass covers the judge read

truths: A refusal echoing a raw token truncates it to a bounded length and strips control characters (a quoted token with an embedded newline cannot inject message-shaped lines)
The unresolvable-target message names the literal-dollar-filename possibility instead of only prescribing variable expansion
In a mixed command the FIRST decisive refusal wording survives — the check_write loop no longer overwrites an earlier denial (guarded by denial.is_none())
New-message tests pin literal fragments, not the message function itself

action: Per CONTEXT.md D3: (a) in hook_local.rs bound the echoed token (e.g. 120 chars + ellipsis) and strip ASCII control chars in unresolvable_bash_target_message and any refusal interpolating a raw token; (b) extend the FIX sentence to name the literal-dollar-filename case; (c) in main.rs guard the check_write loop (previously :313-332) with denial.is_none() so an earlier resolution-failure denial is not overwritten; (d) rewrite the self-referential assert_eq tests (message function as its own expectation) to pin literal message fragments; add a mixed-command test asserting the resolution-failure wording wins.
acceptance: All four must_haves truths hold with named tests; suite green
